document.title: Rules for Granting OIC Consultative Status to Humanitarian Non-Governmental Organizations
document.short_title: OIC Consultative Status Rules for Humanitarian NGOs
document.purpose: Establishes the eligibility requirements, application process, rights, obligations, suspension procedures, and governance for humanitarian NGOs seeking OIC Consultative Status.

charter.description: Charter of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.

secretary_general.description: Head of the OIC General Secretariat.

application.description: Official request submitted by a humanitarian NGO to obtain OIC Consultative Status.

humanitarian_ngo.description: A legally registered humanitarian NGO headquartered in an OIC Member State or an accredited humanitarian organization serving Muslim minorities and communities.

consultative_status.description: Official OIC recognition allowing qualified NGOs to participate in specified OIC meetings and provide humanitarian advice.

mandatory_requirements.description: The NGO must have approval from the government of its headquarters State.
The NGO must be a legally recognized organization.
The NGO must have independent administrative and financial management.
The NGO must maintain transparent administrative and financial auditing systems.
The NGO must be officially registered and licensed.
Headquarters must be located in an OIC Member State OR the NGO must officially represent Muslim minorities or communities.
The NGO must have already carried out humanitarian activities in one or more OIC Member States or for Muslim minorities.
Consultative Status is granted only to the parent organization, not to branches.
The NGO's objectives must not conflict with the OIC Charter.
If the NGO works mainly in another Member State, approval from that State is required.

responsibilities: Circulate eligible applications to Member States at least 90 days before the next Council session.
Prepare a detailed report for the Council.

post_approval_requirement.description: The NGO must immediately inform the General Secretariat whenever its registered activities change.

grounds.reason: Violation of applicable laws or regulations.
Failure to continue meeting eligibility requirements.
Changing organizational activities without reconsideration of status.

coordination.description: NGOs holding Consultative Status must establish a coordination mechanism among themselves.

periodic_meetings.timing: Shortly before ordinary Summit or Council sessions.

rights.right: Deliver brief oral statements based on submitted reports.

workflow.action: Submit application to the General Secretariat.
Secretary General evaluates and prepares recommendations.
Qualified applications are circulated to Member States at least 90 days before the Council session.
Senior Officials Meeting reviews the application.
Council of Foreign Ministers decides by consensus.
Approved NGO receives OIC Consultative Status.
NGO participates in eligible meetings while continuously maintaining compliance.

summary.effective_date: Upon adoption by the Council of Foreign Ministers
